newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault rebounds after Vilvoorde decision.
newsitem.headline: Renault rebounds after Vilvoorde decision.

text.p: Shares in Renault rebounded on Wednesday on relief that the French government did not seem to be pressing the company to keep its Vilvoorde plant open, brokers said.

In an apparent political compromise, the carmaker decided to commission an independent study to explore alternatives to the proposed closure, which Renault insists is essential to streamline its European operations.
"The fact that the government hasn't tried to impose a continuation of the plant's activity will allow Renault to pursue a restructuring," one analyst said.
The stock was up 2.97 percent at 131.60 francs at 1010 GMT after having fallen 4.63 percent on reports of the independent study on Tuesday.
"A fresh examination of the plant's situation by an independent expert represents a good solution," said another analyst. The report is due before the end of the month.

Brokers said the stock was also helped by Chairman Louis Schweitzer's remarks that the breakeven objective for the car division for 1997 looked "reasonably accessible" despite a deterioration in the French market.
If the division were to break even, net and operating results would be positive, he told the annual general meeting.
